title: Linkability of submissions across courses and sessions
description: The portal can link the student's identity, assignment file, course, login event, and submission timestamp across multiple submissions and courses, enabling profiling of the student's behavior and academic activity over time.

uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for linkability due to lack of provided threat-tree catalog.

title: Identifiability of the student from submitted data
description: The submitted data directly contains student id and likely account-authenticated context, making the student readily identifiable from the flow and any associated logs or stored records.
assumptions: Student id is unique and visible to the receiving process or downstream storage/logging.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for identifiability due to lack of provided threat-tree catalog.

title: Submission can be used as evidence against the student
description: The portal may retain records of login and assignment submission, including timestamps and file contents, that can later be used to prove the student's actions or deadlines met/missed, reducing plausible deniability.
assumptions: The system logs authentication and submission events with timestamps.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-repudiation threat due to lack of provided threat-tree catalog.

title: Disclosure of assignment contents and metadata in transit or logs
description: The work file, student id, course, and submission timestamp may be exposed to unauthorized parties if transport protection is weak, endpoints are compromised, or verbose application/network logs capture sensitive payloads and metadata.
assumptions: Sensitive fields may traverse networks and be logged by the application, reverse proxies, or monitoring systems.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for information disclosure due to lack of provided threat-tree catalog.

title: Detectability of student activity from login and submission events
description: Even if content is protected, observers may detect that a particular student is active, enrolled in a course, or submitting at a specific time based on traffic patterns, event timing, or visible metadata.
assumptions: An observer can see communication timing, endpoint access, or coarse metadata even without full content access.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for detectability due to lack of provided threat-tree catalog.

title: Insufficient transparency about collection and use of submission data
description: The student may not be adequately informed about what submission data and metadata are collected, how long files and logs are retained, who can access them, and whether they are used for analytics, plagiarism checks, or auditing.
assumptions: Privacy notices or just-in-time explanations may be incomplete or absent in the portal.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for unawareness due to lack of provided threat-tree catalog.

title: Collection and retention may exceed necessity or policy
description: The portal may collect or retain more personal data than necessary for assignment submission, such as excessive metadata, long-term logs, or unnecessary copies of files, potentially conflicting with privacy principles or institutional policy.
assumptions: Retention limits, minimization controls, or purpose restrictions may be weak or undefined.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-compliance due to lack of provided threat-tree catalog.

title: Linkability of student actions across courses and submissions
description: The portal forwards a stable student identifier together with course and file reference to the grading service, enabling records of submissions and grading requests to be linked across assignments and potentially across courses for the same student.

uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability of messages/records may differ.

title: Identifiability of the student in grading requests
description: The request contains student id and course context, which directly identifies or makes the student readily identifiable to the assignment and grading service and any observers with access to the service-side records.

title: Detectability of student submission activity

uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of transparency/intervenability about data meaning and processing context; node id may be approximate.

title: Sharing student records with parent may exceed consent or legal authorization
description: Displaying the child's grades, feedback, and submission history to a parent may violate policy or legal constraints if the student is old enough to control disclosure, if parental rights are restricted, or if only limited information should be shared.
assumptions: Assumes jurisdictional or institutional rules may limit parental access based on age, custody, consent, or educational privacy obligations.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance due to missing lawful basis/authorization checks; exact node id may vary.

title: Parent can deny having viewed the child's academic records
description: If the system does not maintain adequate access logs or acknowledgements, the parent may later deny having accessed grades, feedback, or submission history, undermining accountability for sensitive record access.
assumptions: Assumes access logging or audit trails are absent, incomplete, or not attributable to the parent account.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for repudiation of performed access/view action; exact numbering may be approximate.

title: Exposure of account and relationship management data to unauthorized portal staff
description: The flow carries names, emails, roles, account status changes, and parent-child relationship data from the administrator into the web app. If the portal does not strictly enforce authorization on administrative functions and stored request data, other internal users or support personnel could learn sensitive identity and family-link information.
assumptions: The web app receives and processes these administration requests and may expose them through admin interfaces, logs, or backend handling.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id chosen as a generic information disclosure node; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary by catalog version.

title: Over-collection of personal data during account and parent-child link administration
description: Administrative account management may request or retain more personal data than necessary for provisioning and relationship management, such as unnecessary identifiers or excessive role/history details. This creates a privacy threat because the web app may process more data than needed for the stated purpose.
assumptions: The portal defines the fields and validation rules for account and relationship administration.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-effort generic detectability/data minimization mapping; exact node naming may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Unclear retention of disabled accounts and historical parent-child links
description: When administrators disable accounts or modify relationships, the web app may keep prior account details and family-link records indefinitely or without clear deletion rules. Retaining obsolete names, emails, roles, and relationship history longer than necessary increases privacy risk.
assumptions: The portal stores account lifecycle events and relationship history after updates or disable actions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id selected for data disclosure/deletion-related retention risk; exact subtree may differ by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Insufficient transparency to affected users about account and relationship changes
description: Students, parents, or guardians may not be informed when an administrator creates an account for them, changes their role, or links/unlinks parent-child relationships. Lack of notice can leave data subjects unaware of processing that materially affects their privacy and access.
assumptions: The portal may not automatically notify affected users of administrative changes.
uncertainty_note: Generic unawareness node chosen; exact node id may vary.

title: Administrative processing may exceed stated purpose or legal basis
description: Using administrator-submitted identity and family relationship data for purposes beyond account provisioning and school communication, or without an appropriate legal basis and policy alignment, creates a non-compliance risk. Parent-child links are particularly sensitive because they encode family relationships.
assumptions: The portal operator is subject to privacy obligations governing purpose limitation, lawful basis, and handling of children's data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic non-compliance node; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

title: Insufficient evidence of who made account and relationship changes
description: If the web app does not maintain trustworthy audit records for create, modify, disable, and link/unlink actions, administrators may later deny having made a change, or affected users may be unable to prove what happened to their account or family linkage data.
assumptions: Administrative actions are security- and privacy-relevant and require accountable logging.
uncertainty_note: Generic non-repudiation node selected; exact subtree may vary.

title: Linkability of identities across family and role records
description: Combining names, emails, roles, and parent-child links in one administrative flow enables the portal to correlate individuals across household, student, parent, and staff contexts. This can make it easier to link records that data subjects may expect to remain contextually separated.
assumptions: The portal stores and can query these attributes together across multiple modules or datasets.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic linkability node; exact node id may differ by threat-tree edition.

title: Linkability of student and parent accounts via stored relationship links
description: The account directory stores explicit parent-child relationship links alongside account records. An attacker or unauthorized internal user who can access directory contents may correlate multiple accounts and infer family relationships, enabling linkage of identities across otherwise separate users.
assumptions: The directory persists relationship identifiers or references that can be queried or read together with account records.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for stored relational linkability may vary.

title: Identifiability of students and guardians from account records
description: Writing account records into the directory may expose directly identifying attributes or stable account identifiers for students and parents/guardians. If the datastore is accessed beyond intended purposes, individuals can be identified from the stored records.
assumptions: Account records contain names, usernames, email addresses, IDs, or other direct/indirect identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability from stored identifying data.

title: Disclosure of sensitive family relationship data in the account directory
description: The grading service writes parent-child relationship links to the account directory. Unauthorized disclosure of these links reveals sensitive household and dependency information, potentially exposing minors' associations with guardians.
assumptions: Relationship links are readable from the datastore and are not fully protected by strict access controls or encryption.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for stored sensitive relationship data.

title: Disclosure of academic-account association through directory writes
description: Because the grading service populates the account directory, the resulting records may reveal that specific identified individuals are participants in the grading/assignment context. This can disclose educational involvement or role information beyond what is necessary for directory operation.
assumptions: Consumers of the directory can infer service participation, role, or educational context from the written records or metadata.
uncertainty_note: Approximate node id; this is disclosure by inference from stored service-linked account data.

title: Unawareness of storage and reuse of parent-child relationship links
description: Students and guardians may be unaware that the grading service writes and persists family relationship links in the account directory, potentially for broader lookup or reuse by other services. This reduces transparency about what relationship data is stored and how it is used.
assumptions: Notices or UI explanations do not clearly explain this write operation and downstream use of relationship links.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for insufficient transparency/unawareness; exact subtree may differ.

title: Non-compliance risk from storing minors' and guardians' relationship data without proper basis or minimization
description: Persisting account records together with parent-child links in the directory may exceed what is necessary for the stated purpose, or may require specific legal basis, retention limits, and protections because it involves minors and family relationship data. If these are not satisfied, the processing may violate privacy obligations.
assumptions: Applicable policy or regulation imposes purpose limitation, data minimization, retention, transparency, or child-data requirements.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for policy/legal non-compliance related to excessive or insufficiently governed storage.

title: Excessive disclosure of student and staff data to third-party host via full backup replication
description: The nightly replication sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to an external cloud hosting provider. This may disclose more personal data than is necessary for backup/hosting purposes, including sensitive educational records and directory information, to a third party.
assumptions: The cloud hosting provider is a separate controller/processor boundary and receives or can access the replicated backup contents in intelligible form.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id is approximate; using a generic disclosure/exposure node because exact LINDDUN Pro subtree labels may vary.

title: Unauthorized access or secondary exposure of replicated backups at cloud provider
description: Once full backups are stored at the cloud hosting provider, provider personnel, co-tenants, attackers, or misconfigured services could gain access to grade records, assignments, and account directory data, causing disclosure of personal data beyond the original educational context.
assumptions: Backups are stored or processed within the provider environment and may be accessible through administrative interfaces, storage services, or support operations.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for disclosure from stored data at recipient/provider side.

title: Cross-dataset linkability of academic records and account directory at provider
description: Combining full grade records, assignment content, and account directory data in one replicated dataset enables the provider environment to link identities, coursework, and performance across systems and time, increasing the ability to correlate records belonging to the same individual.
assumptions: The provider can observe or process multiple replicated datasets or metadata over time.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN Pro node id for linkability may differ; this is a generic best-fit.

title: Identifiability of students and staff from replicated directory and grade data
description: The backup includes account directory information together with grades and assignments, making individuals directly identifiable within the replicated dataset and enabling straightforward attribution of academic records to named persons.
assumptions: Directory data contains direct identifiers such as names, usernames, email addresses, or institutional IDs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic identifiability node; exact subtree may vary.

title: Transfer to cloud provider may be incompatible with purpose limitation or data minimization expectations
description: Sending full educational records and account directory data to a third-party hosting provider for backup/replication may exceed what data subjects expect, especially if the transfer, retention, access model, or jurisdiction is not aligned with the original purpose of grading and assignment management.
assumptions: Applicable policy or legal basis may require minimization, transparency, processor controls, retention limits, or geographic restrictions.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance node id is approximate because exact LINDDUN Pro compliance subtree labels vary.

title: Insufficient transparency to data subjects about third-party backup replication
description: Students and staff may be unaware that their full grade records, assignments, and directory data are replicated nightly to an external cloud hosting provider, reducing their ability to understand processing, retention, and onward access risks.
assumptions: Notices, consent flows, or privacy documentation may omit or insufficiently explain this third-party replication.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit generic unawareness node; exact node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Grade records can be linked across student, parent, and teacher views
description: When the grading service reads the same grade records to construct multiple role-specific views, identifiers and stable record references may allow correlation of a student's performance data across contexts and recipients, enabling linkage of records that should remain context-separated.
assumptions: The service uses common identifiers or shared record keys when generating different views for students, parents, and teachers.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best estimate for linkability via shared identifiers across contexts; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Role-specific views may reveal grade information to unintended parties
description: If the assignment and grading service does not strictly enforce role-based filtering when reading from the grade records database, grade details intended for one audience could become inferable or directly visible in another audience's view, such as exposing broader class performance to parents or parent-only information to teachers.
assumptions: The service dynamically builds different views from the same underlying records and access-control or filtering logic could be flawed.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for information disclosure from insufficient filtering/access control.

title: Students or parents may be identifiable from grade records in generated views
description: The grading service may present names, student numbers, class membership, or other direct or indirect identifiers alongside grades, making the data subject-identifiable to recipients who do not need full identity information.
assumptions: Views include direct identifiers or combinations of attributes sufficient to single out a student.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for identifiability through direct/indirect identifiers in output views.

title: Small cohorts or filtered grade views may enable singling out
description: Even if direct identifiers are removed, the service may generate views for small classes, assignments, or exceptional grades where a student can be singled out based on unique combinations of subject, assignment, score pattern, or class context.
assumptions: Some generated views aggregate or filter records over small groups or unusual performance patterns.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for identifiability/singling out from quasi-identifiers and small populations.

title: Grade records may be reused beyond the original educational purpose
description: Reading grade records to build multiple stakeholder views can exceed the original purpose for which the records were collected if the scope of disclosure to parents, teachers, or other viewers is not aligned with consent, policy, or educational necessity.
assumptions: Purpose limitation, consent, or policy constraints exist on how grade records may be repurposed for different audiences.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for non-compliance with purpose limitation or lawful basis constraints.

title: Data subjects may be unaware of how grade records are shared across views
description: Students and possibly parents may not understand that the grading service reads the central grade database to generate multiple role-based views, what exact data elements are shown to each audience, and under what rules, reducing transparency.
assumptions: The system does not clearly communicate data flows, recipients, or view-generation logic to data subjects.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for lack of transparency/unawareness about processing and recipients.

title: Insufficient evidence of who accessed which grade records for which view
description: If reads from the grade records database are not logged with sufficient detail, the organization may be unable to prove whether a student's grades were accessed appropriately for a student, parent, or teacher view, undermining accountability and enabling repudiation of access events.
assumptions: Read access logging, audit trails, or purpose-of-access records may be incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id for repudiation due to inadequate auditability of data access.
